title: Docker image for the upstream Linux build (no downloaded FFmpeg binaries)
description: Write an ORBIS Dockerfile on ubuntu:24.04 using packages_debian and the commands in .forgemesh/research/build-deps.json. Configure downloads FFmpeg binaries unless FFMPEG_PREBUILT_DIR is set (BUILD.md line 77), which breaks the no-binaries rule. Find out how 3rdparty/ffmpeg-core produces its package and either build it from source in a separate stage or document why that is not possible.
acceptance: docker build completes the configure and `cmake --build build` on a clean checkout of upstream main at a pinned SHA
Configure log shows no FFmpeg download, or the task report states exactly which artifact is downloaded and from where
Image pins the upstream SHA and records the submodule SHAs (`git submodule status`)

title: Reproduce the upstream lavapipe test baseline inside the container
description: Run ctest with the release.yml settings (ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1, GALLIUM_OVERRIDE_CPU_CAPS=avx, --timeout 120, -E '^precise_wait$') on mesa-vulkan-drivers lavapipe. Record pass/fail per test as the ORBIS baseline for main. Expected known issues: write-watch tests need host kernel >= 6.7; four native depth tests fail without /dev/udmabuf (#23709); agc_driver_scattered_runs and agc_driver_image_table_packed_guards fail on some upstream runners (#24834).
acceptance: JUnit XML and ctest log stored as a baseline artifact with the upstream SHA and Mesa version (dpkg-query -W mesa-vulkan-drivers)
Each failure is classified: environment (kernel, udmabuf), known upstream issue (with issue number), or new
Tests over 30 s are listed (CONTRIBUTING.md limit)

title: Upstream sync job: track main and open PR metadata read-only
description: Upstream merges about 1000 commits per day to main (790 commits since 2026-11-24 per the commits API on 2026-11-25) and has 2666 open PRs. Build a scheduled read-only fetch of main and of open PR metadata (number, title, author, labels, head SHA, Fixes/Unblocks/Depends lines) with gh api pagination, under a fixed call budget. No writes to upstream.
acceptance: Job uses only GET requests and records rate-limit usage per run
Output is a JSONL snapshot comparable across runs (new, closed, merged and label changes)
ORBIS main fast-forwards from upstream main without local divergence, or the divergence is reported

title: Choose a winner in each duplicate-PR cluster with a Fixes reference
description: Clusters in .forgemesh/research/pr-clusters.json where several open PRs reference the same issue: #15234 (15242, 21451, 26698), #26881 (23014, 27123), #22509 (22510, 26696), #25225 (25226, 25279), #23485 (23486, 24987), #11977 (12316, 22382), #14439 (14944, 19852), #23480 (23787, 26690), #15742 (20580, 26221). For each cluster, diff the candidates, check whether the linked issue is still open, and pick one with reasons. Read-only: no comments upstream.
acceptance: One decision record per cluster: chosen PR, rejected PRs, reasons, linked issue state
The chosen PR merges cleanly into the current ORBIS main, or the conflict is described
Tests added or changed by the chosen PR pass in the ORB-002 container

title: Evaluate the 212-PR 'drop redundant errno saves' series as one unit
description: sschandra2006 has 212 open refactor PRs (130 titled 'drop redundant errno saves around guest copies'; 200 opened on 2026-11-25) and 35 merged. Sampled PRs are tiny deletions (26941: 1 file, -3 lines; 27036: 1 file, -3 lines). Check that the removed errno saves are really redundant: does the guest copy helper already preserve errno on every path, including fault paths? Decide whether ORBIS takes the series, a subset, or none.
acceptance: Written argument, with code references, on whether the guest copy helper preserves errno on success and on fault
At least 5 PRs from the series are applied together and the affected library tests pass
Recommendation: take all, take a subset (with the list), or reject

title: Pick one implementation per duplicated libSceLibreSsl3/libcurl export
description: Duplicate pairs with identical titles: SSL_is_quic (16589, 17843), SSL_set_quic_transport_params (16981, 19125), EC_POINT_dup (17621, 19044), ECDSA_do_sign (17626, 21684), curl_formget (17661, 22996). GalaxyGamingFR's versions carry 'needs rebase'. Compare them against the upstream LibreSSL/curl semantics in 3rdparty and pick one per export.
acceptance: Per export: chosen PR and a short semantic comparison against the bundled LibreSSL or curl source
The chosen PRs merge together without conflict on ORBIS main
Debt fragments in docs/dev/debt/changes are consistent with the change

title: Run the AMD Polaris / pre-RDNA2 failing AGC tests on real hardware
description: Open upstream issues: #9759 (agc_driver_sample_order_recipe_depth_locations fails on RADV Polaris) and #15316 (agc_driver_f32_fma_denormal_mode2 fails on RADV before RDNA2: Mesa splits GLSL Fma). Closed related: #9781 (agc_idle_publish_wait on RADV Polaris). Re-run these tests on ORBIS main on a Polaris card (RX 470/480/570/580) with RADV and record the Mesa version, so ORBIS knows whether they still fail.
acceptance: Host report (ANYPS5_HOST_REPORT=1) attached: GPU, driver, Mesa and kernel version
Pass/fail for agc_driver_sample_order_recipe_depth_locations, agc_driver_f32_fma_denormal_mode2 and agc_idle_publish_wait, with logs
Vulkan validation-layer run (>= 1.4.335) with the VUID- count

title: GPU-change gate: validation-layer diff and GPU list for integrated PRs
description: CONTRIBUTING.md requires GPU changes (AGC, shader recompiler, VideoOut) to have validation-layer runs on main and on the change with no new VUID- errors, plus the vendor/model/driver/OS of each GPU tested. Only 645 of 2559 parsed open PR bodies have a non-n/a 'GPUs tested' line. Wire tools/vulkan_validation_gate.py into the ORBIS integration pipeline so no agc/shader PR is integrated without that evidence.
acceptance: The gate runs on lavapipe in the ORB-002 container on main and on a candidate PR and reports new VUIDs
ORBIS refuses to integrate a PR labelled agc or shader without a GPUs-tested record (upstream's or ORBIS's own)
Documented how the gate differs from upstream usage, if it does

title: Batch-merge test of the upstream 'review queue' PRs
description: Upstream labels the 30 oldest ready PRs 'review queue' every hour (30 open on 2026-11-25, e.g. 26630, 26601, 26600, 26521, 26221, 26182, 26036, 26034, 21969, 22140, 22251, 22328). Upstream CI can merge up to 40 PRs together (build.yml workflow_dispatch input 'pr'). Reproduce that locally: merge the queue in order onto ORBIS main, run tools/pr_overlap.py and tools/select_tests.py, and report conflicts and failing tests per PR.
acceptance: Merge order and per-PR result (clean, conflict, test failure) recorded
pr_overlap.py output saved for the batch
Selected tests pass, or failures are attributed to a specific PR

title: Map dependency chains for the 'Unblocks title' PR series
description: 108 open PRs carry 'unblocks title' and 373 PR bodies contain 'Depends on #N'. Several titles have 4-7 PRs (PPSA01317, PPSA26344, PPSA99169, CUSA00900, PPSA02015, CUSA00223). Build a dependency graph from the Depends on/Unblocks lines and produce an ordered merge plan per title.
acceptance: Graph (JSON) of PR -> depends-on PRs for all open PRs, with closed/merged dependencies marked
Ordered plan for each title with >= 4 PRs
Cycles or dependencies on closed-unmerged PRs are flagged

title: Triage needs-rebase and long-idle open PRs
description: 523 open PRs carry 'needs rebase' (229 created before 2026-11-11), 133 are older than 30 days, and 20 were not updated since 2026-11-18. 5 are labelled 'already in main' (7704, 22162, 22468, 22595, 23060) and 9138 is the only 'stale' one. Classify the old ones: superseded by a merged PR, superseded by an open duplicate, or still useful and rebasable by ORBIS.
acceptance: List of PRs older than 30 days with one class each and evidence (merged PR number, duplicate, or rebase result)
'already in main' PRs excluded from every ORBIS integration list
No upstream interaction

title: Licence inventory of the 39 submodules and FidelityFX-FSR
description: Upstream is GPL-2.0-only. GitHub's licence API identifies only some submodules (e.g. SDL Zlib, SPIRV-Tools Apache-2.0, VulkanMemoryAllocator MIT, ffmpeg-core LGPL-2.1, libusb-cmake LGPL-2.1, mimalloc MIT); many are NOASSERTION, libressl/openbsd returned 404, and pixman, cairo and libyuv are not on GitHub. Read the licence file at each pinned submodule SHA and flag combinations to check for GPL-2.0-only compatibility (notably Apache-2.0 and the LibreSSL/OpenSSL-family licences).
acceptance: Table: submodule, pinned SHA, licence file path, SPDX identifier
Potential GPL-2.0-only incompatibilities listed for human (legal) review, without conclusions stated as fact
Licences of the submodules' own nested submodules checked, or noted as not checked

title: ORBIS CONTRIBUTING and NOTICE: fork status, AI disclosure, no upstream endorsement
description: Write ORBIS docs that state it is an independent collaborative fork of boykopovar/AnyPS5, not endorsed by upstream or by Sony (upstream README already disclaims Sony affiliation), and that ORBIS does not open PRs or comments upstream on its own. Carry over the upstream rules ORBIS relies on: Conventional Commits, no code comments except debt markers, 30 s test limit, the GPU-testing evidence, and the AI disclosure line 'AI-assisted: yes / no' (upstream: 'Say whether the change was written with AI assistance. The author of the pull request is responsible for every line of it.').
acceptance: Docs contain a non-endorsement statement and a link to upstream
Upstream rules are quoted with their source path, not paraphrased as ORBIS's own
Every ORBIS agent commit or PR template has an AI-assisted field

title: Track the upstream main Linux CI failure on anyps5-2 runners (#24834)
description: Issue #24834 (opened 2026-11-21): agc_driver_scattered_runs and agc_driver_image_table_packed_guards fail on every main Linux job on the anyps5-2 runners since 17 Nov, and pass on anyps5-3. Find out whether the ORB-002 container reproduces it and which host property (CPU, Mesa, kernel) matters, so ORBIS does not blame integrated PRs for it.
acceptance: Reproduced or not reproduced in the ORBIS container, with Mesa version and CPU model
Both tests added to an ORBIS known-failure list with the issue number if they fail on main
Host properties that differ between passing and failing runs listed
